Local symbols (flagged to the editor): $x^{\mathrm{A}}_{1,i}$ the $x_1$ centroid of an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face of cell $i$
on the face's own measure [m]; $(\sigma^{\mathrm{A}}_i)^2$ the second central moment of $x_1$ on that measure
[m$^2$]; $\delta^{\mathrm{A}}_i = x_{1,i} - x^{\mathrm{A}}_{1,i}$ the face-centroid shift [m]; $I_n$ the integral
$\int_{r_-}^{r_+} r^n\,\mathrm{d}r$ [m$^{n+1}$].

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: the exact $x_1$ second moment of an $x_2$/$x_3$ face and the exact distance between a cell's volume
centroid and that face's centroid, in a cancellation-free form. **Switch**: read only when `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` is
set (@sec-ch12-flux-covariance). **Default**: off at the pin, on since chengcli/snapy#307 (the helpers exist on
every grid). **Requires**: nothing. **Order**: exact. **Defining equations**: @eq-ch03-facemoments-moment,
@eq-ch03-facemoments-shift. **Zero-shift flag** (main after chengcli/snapy#308): a host constant of the coordinate type
that says the shift is identically zero, so the covariance skips its centroid parts; a tripwire test keeps the flag
equal to the shift.
:::

Text and rows marked "main after chengcli/snapy#308" were checked against main at
snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5; the rest of this section's text was checked at
snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0. Code citations resolve at the pin of `code_pin.yml`.

The flux through an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face is a face average, weighted by the face's own area measure. On a Cartesian
grid that weight is uniform in $x_1$; on the spherical-polar and cubed-sphere grids an $x_2$/$x_3$ face spans
$r\,\mathrm{d}r$ times an angular factor while the cell spans $r^2\,\mathrm{d}r$ times one. Two numbers follow from
the face measure: its $x_1$ variance, which sets the size of the covariance of two fields over the face, and the
offset between where a cell average lives and where the face average lives. Both enter the $O(\Delta x_1^2)$ face-flux
corrections of @sec-ch04. This scheme supplies them exactly; the flux use is in @sec-ch04. In the history it is part
of [chengcli/snapy#289](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/issues/289) and its follow-up items.

### Derivation

The derivation is in {{< code docs/derivations/289-covariance-x3-curved.md >}}
§2.7 (the moment) and §2A.1 (the two centroids); it is rewritten here in the report's notation. The angular factor
of an $x_2$/$x_3$ face does not vary along $x_1$ on one face, so it cancels in every average and the face weight is
$w(r) = r$. With $h = h_i$ and $x^{\mathrm{m}} = x^{\mathrm{m}}_{1,i} = \tfrac12(r_- + r_+)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
x^{\mathrm{A}}_{1,i} &= \frac{I_2}{I_1} = \frac{12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 + h^2}{12\,x^{\mathrm{m}}}, \\
x_{1,i} &= \frac{I_3}{I_2} = \frac{3x^{\mathrm{m}}\left(4(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 + h^2\right)}{12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 + h^2},
\end{aligned}
$$

the second being the spherical-polar volume centroid of @eq-ch03-sphpolar-centroids. The second central moment on the
face measure is $(I_3 - 2x^{\mathrm{A}}I_2 + (x^{\mathrm{A}})^2I_1)/I_1$, which simplifies to

$$
(\sigma^{\mathrm{A}}_i)^2 = \frac{h^2}{12}\left(1 - \frac{h^2}{12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2}\right).
$$ {#eq-ch03-facemoments-moment}

@eq-ch03-facemoments-moment is `radial_face_moment2_` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::radial_face_moment2_ >}}). Subtracting the two
centroids directly would cancel, because both are close to $x^{\mathrm{m}}$; doing the algebra first gives the exact

$$
\delta^{\mathrm{A}}_i = \frac{h^2\left(12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 - h^2\right)}{12\,x^{\mathrm{m}}\left(12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 + h^2\right)}
= \frac{h^2}{12\,x^{\mathrm{m}}} + O\!\left(\frac{h^4}{(x^{\mathrm{m}})^3}\right).
$$ {#eq-ch03-facemoments-shift}

@eq-ch03-facemoments-shift is `radial_face_centroid_shift_` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::radial_face_centroid_shift_ >}}). On a Cartesian grid
the two measures are the same uniform weight, so the moment is $h^2/12$ and the shift is zero; these are the base-class
values `face_moment2_x1` and `face_centroid_shift_x1` ([`coordinate.cpp:442-465`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L442-L465)). Both formulas are exact,
not truncated; @eq-ch03-facemoments-moment recovers $h^2/12$ as $h/x^{\mathrm{m}}\to0$.

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
`geometry_check.py`, lines `[C1]` to `[C3]` of `geometry_check.out`: the centroids, the moment and the shift
against the exact integrals, exact symbolic (sympy).
:::

### Numerical method

Both helpers return one value per $x_1$ cell, ghosts included, shaped like `dx1f`, from the face array alone. A face
with $x^{\mathrm{m}}\le h/2$ (an $x_1$ ghost that reaches $r\le0$) is degenerate: the moment's curvature correction
and the shift are set to zero there, and the divisors are clamped to $10^{-300}$ so the masked branch never divides by
zero. Spherical-polar and gnomonic grids override the virtual methods to call the radial forms; on the gnomonic grid
the cell volume is the same $r^2$ integral times the solid angle (@sec-ch03-gnomonic), so the same shift applies even
though its `x1v` is the midpoint. They are evaluated when the covariance correction asks for them, in the stage, before
the $x_2$/$x_3$ fluxes. @fig-ch03-facemoments-ratio plots both against $h/x^{\mathrm{m}}$.

*The zero-shift flag (main after chengcli/snapy#308).* On the base measure the shift is zero by construction:
`face_centroid_shift_x1` returns `zeros_like(dx1f)` unconditionally ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::face_centroid_shift_x1 >}}). Every centroid part
of the covariance is then an exact zero, so since chengcli/snapy#308 the covariance asks a second virtual,
`face_centroid_shift_zero` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateImpl::face_centroid_shift_zero >}}), and skips those parts when it is true. It is a literal of the
coordinate type, not a test of tensor contents: `true` in the base class, so Cartesian inherits it; `false` in
`SphericalPolarImpl` (`face_centroid_shift_zero`, {{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.hpp SphericalPolarImpl::face_centroid_shift_zero >}}) and `GnomonicEquiangleImpl`
(`face_centroid_shift_zero`, {{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.hpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::face_centroid_shift_zero >}}), the two classes that override the shift; and `false` in
`CylindricalImpl` (`face_centroid_shift_zero`, {{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CylindricalImpl::face_centroid_shift_zero >}}). Cylindrical builds no `dx1f`, so the base
shift has nothing to take `zeros_like` of, and its faces are $r$-weighted, so its shift is not zero in general; with
`false` it keeps the path main took before. The flag is read in three places: the centroid parts of
`_flux_covariance` (`centroid`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::_flux_covariance >}}), the same in `scalar_flux_covariance` (`centroid`,
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::scalar_flux_covariance >}}), and the shifted pressure of the geometric source (`face_centroid_shift_zero`,
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). Because the flag comes from the type, no class can return zeros only for some grids,
and it holds no state that a re-mesh or `.to()` could leave stale [source: chengcli/snapy#308 body, commits 4 and 5].

The guard changes no arithmetic order. The #308 body reports, for commit 4 against its base with
`SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=1` and `gravity-work: face`: `hydro_u`, `hydro_w` and the step sizes `torch.equal` and equal
as int64 bit patterns on an A100 (2-D $120\times178$, 200 steps; $160^3$, 20 steps) and on CPU (the 2-D deck);
`test_scalar_flux_covariance.py` bit-identical on Cartesian and gnomonic-equiangle, CPU and CUDA, covariance off and
on; on top of commits 1-3, the six-panel moist positivity deck, 40 cycles, 498 saved tensors, 0 differ; and ctest
`-R 'covariance|positivity'` 15/15, `-R 'covariance|positivity|lu_failure|gravity_work_cache|coordinate'` 18/18 on
both builds. Commit 5 changes only the cylindrical flag and the test, so in `src/` no Cartesian or gnomonic-equiangle
path changes [source: chengcli/snapy#308 body, Evidence; sha: the commits named there, squash-merged as
snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5; run: A100 and CPU builds, not re-run here]. The step time and kernel counts of the same
runs belong to @sec-ch14 and are not repeated here.

*A lesson from the same PR.* A positivity-carry change that read the velocity from `w` was dropped from
chengcli/snapy#308: on gnomonic-equiangle grids `w` holds the contravariant tangential velocity while the carry's rows
are covariant, so it is not $u/\rho$ there [source: chengcli/snapy#308 body]. A shortcut that is exact on Cartesian
and spherical-polar grids can be wrong on the cubed sphere for a reason that a Cartesian bitwise comparison cannot
see; the dropped change is described only in the body, and no test in the repository encodes the distinction
(**missing evidence**).

Both are dimensionless and tend to $1$ as the cell becomes thin; the moment is the Cartesian one to within $h^2/(12(x^{\\mathrm{m}})^2)$."

: Code map of the radial face moments. {#tbl-ch03-facemoments-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-facemoments-code):

1. The caller asks the coordinate for `face_moment2_x1` and `face_centroid_shift_x1`; virtual dispatch picks the
   grid's form ([`spherical_polar.cpp:213-222`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L213-L222)).
2. `radial_face_moment2_` forms $h$ and $x^{\mathrm{m}}$ from the faces and masks the degenerate cells with
   `torch::where` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::radial_face_moment2_ >}}).
3. `radial_face_centroid_shift_` evaluates the cancellation-free quotient and masks the same cells
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::radial_face_centroid_shift_ >}}).

| `test_radial_face_moments` | the closed forms equal the rationals | $10^{-14}$ relative | a few operations of round-off |
| `test_radial_face_moments` | per-cell indexing on a four-cell column | $10^{-14}$ abs., $10^{-12}$ rel. | as above, and the integrals' cancellation |
| `test_coordinate` (main after #308) | `face_centroid_shift_zero_matches_the_shift`: the flag equals "the shift is all zero" for each coordinate type, in float64 and float32; cylindrical's flag is `false` | exact (boolean) | the test's `EXPECT_EQ` |

: Tests of the radial face moments. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-facemoments-tests}

The cases are `the_rationals_are_the_integrals`, `closed_forms_match_the_exact_integrals` and
`one_value_per_cell_on_a_multi_cell_column` ([`test_radial_face_moments.cpp:49-91`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_radial_face_moments.cpp#L49-L91)); the cells
$[1.5, 2.5]$, $[3, 5]$, $[1, 2]$ have shift $47/1176$, $47/588$, $13/252$ and moment $47/576$, $47/144$,
$13/162$, as listed in `kCells` ({{< code tests/test_radial_face_moments.cpp kCells >}}). These rationals are reproduced
exactly by line `[C2]` of `geometry_check.out`. The test runs on CPU, one process; the helpers are pure tensor
functions with no device-specific path. Its pass status at the pin was not run for this chapter (missing evidence).

*The tripwire (main after chengcli/snapy#308).* `face_centroid_shift_zero_matches_the_shift`
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp Coordinate.face_centroid_shift_zero_matches_the_shift >}}, in `test_coordinate`, {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}) builds a block of each coordinate type, cartesian,
cylindrical, spherical-polar and gnomonic-equiangle, on a radius range of 1 to 2, in float64 and again after
`.to(float32)`. For the three types that build a shift it requires `face_centroid_shift_zero()` to be true exactly
when `face_centroid_shift_x1()` is all zero, and the shift to have the block's dtype; for cylindrical, which builds
none, it requires the flag to be `false`. A new type that overrides the shift without the flag fails it. The #308
body reports that the test passes at the head (CPU build) and fails on spherical-polar when `SphericalPolarImpl`'s flag
is forced to `true` [source: chengcli/snapy#308 body, Evidence]. Linfeng Li's review run of the final #308 head
(snapy@7b5dd2093bbac05408309287390e59edf4088fc8, whose tree is that of snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5; CPU build, one scratch copy per
broken flag) also forced the base class's flag to `false`: the test then fails on cartesian, so it fires on both
broken flags [source: review run, not in the #308 body; deck: the test itself]. No run with cylindrical's flag forced
to `true` is recorded (**missing evidence**), although the test asserts `false` for it directly.

### Limits

No known limits beyond the degenerate-face mask, which drops the curvature correction on ghost cells that reach
$r \le 0$, and, since chengcli/snapy#308, one rule: the zero-shift flag is a host constant that nothing checks against
the device at run time. A coordinate type that overrides `face_centroid_shift_x1` must also return `false` from
`face_centroid_shift_zero`, or the covariance drops its centroid parts on that grid; only the tripwire test above
enforces this. The helpers are used only by `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE`; their effect on the solution belongs to @sec-ch04. The
switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
